entities.summary: The Old Man and the Sea is a 1952 short novel by Ernest Hemingway, written between December 1950 and February 1951. This novella tells the story of Santiago, an aging fisherman, and his harrowing journey to catch a giant marlin off the coast of Cuba. Hemingway's sparse prose and themes of perseverance and human struggle against nature have made this work a classic of modernist literature. The novella explores the relationship between man and nature, as well as the passage of time and the human condition. It has been widely acclaimed for its literary merit and has been translated into many languages. The Old Man and the Sea has been adapted into numerous stage and film productions, cementing its place in popular culture. Hemingway's own life and experiences as a fisherman and writer are deeply intertwined with the narrative, adding to the work's authenticity and emotional resonance.
